subject: Communication
title: The Power of Paraphrasing
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Power of Paraphrasing.

hook.text: 'So what you're saying is...' — six words that transform a conversation.

buildup.text: Paraphrasing restates the speaker's message in your own words. It verifies understanding and shows genuine engagement.

discovery.text: Negotiation research shows that paraphrasing increases agreement rates by 30%.

twist.text: Parroting (repeating exact words) isn't paraphrasing. Effective paraphrasing captures the meaning and emotion.

climax.text: Paraphrasing helps the listener too. Restating ideas in your words deepens comprehension and memory of the exchange.

punchline.text: Repeat their words and they feel heard. Restate their meaning and they feel understood.

quiz.question: How much does paraphrasing increase agreement rates in negotiations?

details.summary: Paraphrasing restates the speaker's message in your own words to confirm understanding. It shows you are listening, catches misunderstandings early, and makes the speaker feel valued. Effective paraphrasing captures both the content and the emotion behind the message.
details.whyItMatters: Paraphrasing is the single most practical listening tool. It prevents miscommunication, builds trust, and deepens understanding in every conversation.
takeaways: Restate the speaker's message in your own words
Capture both factual content and underlying emotion
Paraphrasing catches misunderstandings before they compound

faq.question: How often should you paraphrase in a conversation?
faq.answer: After major points, when the topic shifts, when emotions are high, or when instructions are complex. Over-paraphrasing feels patronizing. In professional settings, summarizing after every two to three minutes of complex discussion is a good rhythm.

faq.question: What is a good paraphrasing formula to start with?
faq.answer: Start with so what I'm hearing is or it sounds like you're saying followed by your understanding. End with did I get that right to invite correction. This three-part structure confirms content, shows engagement, and opens space for clarification.
